'''''Laguncularia''''' is a genus of plants in the family [[Combretaceae]]. The only species in the genus is '''''Laguncularia racemosa''''',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://plants.usda.gov/home/plantProfile?symbol=LAGUN2|title=Classification for Kingdom Plantae Down to Genus ''Laguncularia''|website=United States Department of Agriculture|access-date=18 February 2023}}</ref> the '''white mangrove'''.<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" />

It is native to the coasts of western Africa from Senegal to Cameroon, the Atlantic Coast of the Americas from Bermuda and Florida to the Bahamas, Mexico, the Caribbean, and south to Brazil; and on the Pacific Coast of the Americas from Mexico to northwestern Peru, including the [[Galápagos Islands]].<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" />

[[Image:Laguncularia racemosa flowers.jpg|thumb|Flowers]]
It is a [[mangrove]] tree, growing to {{convert|12|-|18|m|ft|abbr=on}} tall. The [[Bark (botany)|bark]] is gray-brown or reddish, and rough and fissured. [[Aerial root#Pneumatophores|Pneumatophores]] and/or prop roots may be present, depending on environmental conditions. The [[leaf|leaves]] are opposite, elliptical, {{convert|12|-|18|cm|in|abbr=on}} long, and {{convert|2.5|-|5.0|cm|in|abbr=on}} broad, rounded at both ends, entire, smooth, leathery in texture, slightly fleshy, without visible veins, and yellow-green in color. The [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]] is stout, reddish, and {{convert|10|-|13|mm|in|abbr=on}} long, with two small glands near the blade that exude sugars. The white, bell-shaped [[flower]]s are mostly [[plant sexuality|bisexual]] and about {{convert|5|mm|in|abbr=on}} long.  The [[fruit]] is a reddish-brown [[drupe]], about {{convert|12|-|20|mm|in|abbr=on}} long, with longitudinal ridges. The single seed is sometimes [[vivipary#In plants|viviparous]].

It grows in coastal areas of bays, [[lagoon]]s, and [[Creek (tidal)|tidal creek]]s, typically growing inland of other mangroves, well above the high tide line.
